title: Hiring Decisions Cookbook — Risk Signals & Calibration Checklist (beta)
content:
Purpose:
This is a practical, lightweight cookbook to help hiring managers, recruiters, and interviewers surface and calibrate hiring risk signals during the interview funnel, and to translate those signals into concrete hiring and onboarding mitigations.

Scope and intended use:
- Covers mid-senior IC and manager hires across Eng / Product / Design.
- Intended to be used during debriefs and offer decision moments (pre-offer and offer-with-conditions).
- Not a replacement for formal interview rubrics or legal/comp requirements; complements existing scorecards.

Quick navigation (TL;DR):
- Stage-by-stage checklist (screen -> onsite -> debrief)
- Top 12 risk signals and recommended mitigations
- Mini-rubric: translating qualitative signals into a 1–5 risk band
- Offer templates for: standard, conditional, and trial-contracts
- Onboarding shortcuts if hire accepted under mitigation plan

Stage-by-stage checklist (short):
- Recruiter screen: confirm role expectations, must-have vs nice-to-have, candidate constraints (visa, notice), flag any resume gaps.
- Hiring manager 1: technical baseline + red flags log. Note: if candidate declines small coding exercise, mark and probe.
- Cross-functional interview: look for collaboration signals and product judgment; capture concrete examples.
- Culture/manager fit: ask for 2 failure stories and 2 examples of mentoring/feedback.
- Debrief: fill risk-band, escalate >3 high-risk signals to hiring panel.

Top risk signals (observed behavior -> what it usually means -> recommended action):
1) Vague impact stories -> may inflate prior role; require artifact proof (PRs, metrics screenshots) or follow-up work sample.
2) Short tenures across multiple companies (<=12 months, 3+ roles) -> potential flight risk; ask for context, discuss expected comp/role stability, consider trial contract.
3) Avoidance of ownership examples -> likely not comfortable with end-to-end scope; choose a role-aligned onboarding plan with early small ownership milestones.
4) Defensive answers during feedback questions -> growth mindset risk; include manager follow-up about coaching approach and set explicit 30/60/90 deliverables.
5) Declines pair programming or take-home -> toolchain mismatch or time constraints; offer alternative live pairing or time-boxed take-home.
6) Over-reliance on academic language or theoretical answers without applied examples -> weaker production experience; request code walkthrough or systems post-mortem.
7) Overconfidence on unfamiliar systems -> look for pattern of bluffing; schedule technical lead follow-up on specific areas.
8) Notice period >8 weeks + no contingency plan -> potential start-date risks; consider interim coverage plan or later start date in offer.
9) Work authorization ambiguity -> legal risk; coordinate early with people-ops and immigration counsel.
10) Frequent contract-to-contract transitions with gaps -> may indicate preference for short-term work; discuss incentives and retention levers.
11) Cultural misalignment language (e.g., repeatedly frames decisions as "my way") -> cross-check with behavioral anchors and references.
12) Reference mismatch (refers to senior-level stories but ref calls below that) -> probe for seniority inflation; request an additional reference.

Mini risk rubric (how to convert notes into a 1–5 band):
- 1 (Low risk): clear, objective examples; artifacts provided; corroborated by references.
- 2 (Low-medium): minor gaps can be closed with onboarding; expressed learning orientation.
- 3 (Medium): one or two notable risk signals; recommend conditional offer or stronger onboarding.
- 4 (High): multiple red flags or contradictions; require hiring panel escalation and/or trial contract.
- 5 (Reject): significant mismatch to role fundamentals or compliance/legal issues.

Decision templates (short snippets to copy into debrief):
- Standard green: "Recommend hire. Candidate demonstrates required technical baseline, ownership examples, and strong collaborative signals. No material risk flags."
- Conditional offer suggestion: "Recommend hire conditioned on completion of X (e.g., take-home, reference, or specific certification) within 30 days of start OR 90-day performance plan. See mitigation plan attached."
- Trial/contract-first: "Recommend offer as a 3-month contractor with completion milestones and conversion criteria. Rationale: multiple short-tenure signals and onboarding budget to validate retention."

Onboarding mitigations (examples mapped to signals):
- Short tenures/flight risk: set 30/60/90 milestone tied to meaningful deliverables and quarterly check-ins with manager + retention conversations.
- Ownership gap: oriented ramp to own a small, well-scoped component within first 30 days with clear success criteria.
- Feedback defensiveness: structure weekly 1:1s focusing on feedback acceptance and coach-in-role plan.
- System knowledge gap: schedule dedicated buddy rotations and 2-week shadow period across infra/ops team.

Reference and evidence checklist (before offer):
- At least one reference that directly supervised candidate for a similar scope.
- Artifacts that map to the claims in the resume (PR links, metrics, designs).
- Confirmed eligibility to work and tentative start date.

Operational notes (practicalities):
- If role requires compliance (SOC2/Finance/Customer PII), escalate to security & legal early — these are firm blockers.
- When in doubt, prefer conditional offer with explicit conversion criteria vs. "soft trust".
- Use JIRA-PEOPLE-88 template (linked_artifacts above) for conditional offers so legal has a trail.

Sample interview prompts (short, copyable):
- "Tell me about a time you inherited a messy codebase and shipped a production fix; what metrics changed and how did you measure impact?"
- "Describe a decision where you changed your mind after new data; what did you do and what was the outcome?"
- "Walk me through a recent PR you authored that took the most back-and-forth; what was the hardest feedback and how did you respond?"

Reference questions to ask (manager refs):
- What measurable impact did the candidate have in the first 6 months?
- How did the candidate handle conflicting priorities? Provide an example.
- Is there any reason you would not rehire?

Notes-to-self / open questions (WIP):
- Add manager 30/60/90 template for conditional offers (Tara to draft) — TODO by 2026-02-10.
- Need a short FAQ for candidates offered trial-contracts; legal to review.
- Consider a lightweight score normalization table for the panel (Jon to prototype).

Appendix: quick offer wording examples (copy/paste friendly)
- Standard: "We are excited to offer you the role X at Redwood Inference. This offer is contingent on standard checks and our mutual alignment on start date."
- Conditional: "We are pleased to offer you role X subject to completion of [artifact/condition] within 30 days of start. Completion will be reviewed by your manager against agreed success criteria."
- Trial contract: "We propose an initial 3-month contract to validate fit. Key milestones and conversion criteria will be defined in writing prior to start."

Endnotes / links to follow-up resources:
- People-ops conditional offer template (JIRA-PEOPLE-88)
- Interview rubric canonical page (CONFR-3124)
- Slack thread for calibration experiments (linked above)

Rough metadata / provenance:
- Drafted from 1:1s with hiring managers across eng & product, and input from legal and SRE.
- Beta rollout plan: pilot on two eng hires in Q1 2026, measure time-to-offer and early retention.

If you're reading this and want to iterate: add concrete examples, attach anonymized interview notes (redact PII), and let's reduce friction for managers who want a fast, defensible decision."
